I started walking down Kingston, when I heard something ringing. At first, I thought it was just an after-effect of all the blaring music of the parade. But after I wiggled my finger in my ear once, twice, three times—but the ringing continued, I was quite confused. The friend I was walking with turned to me, “Sruli, your pocket’s ringing.” “Hu? What could be ringing in my pocket?” I wondered aloud. But when I slid my hand into my right jacket pocket, I realized that he was right; the ringing noise was coming from a phone after all! There’s just one problem with that: I don’t own a cell phone! Nor did I have any idea how this one ended up in my jacket pocket! “Hello?” I asked quizzically. “Sruli, hi. It’s me, Noam.” “Mr. Mikhailov? But how did you—I mean how did I get this—” “Sruli, I’ve been trying to get in touch with you all day. Realizing that it would be exceedingly difficult for Rabbi Benjaminson to get you into his office today,

home after all the festivities, I just asked an employee of mine to drop a cell

you a buzz when the parade ended.” My head was spinning. Mr. Mikhailov continued, “Sruli, I wanted to ask you something.” Pretending that I wasn’t totally baffled that such a thing was normal for him— besides for being in complete bewilderment as to how a cell phone had slipped into my pocket unnoticed—I responded, “Absolutely, Mr. Mikhailov. How can I help you?” “Shavuos is coming up very soon. You know what I’m thinking?” “Ten Commandments?” I asked. “Yes. And ice cream.The biggest ice cream party the world has ever seen. And as for the party guests, I will leave that up to you.” “It’s so cool that you said that, Mr. Mikhailov.” “Go on,” he requested. “You see,” I explained, “The Rebbe said that Shavuos is a holiday especially for us kids. When Hashem was ready to give the Torah to the Jewish people, He asked for a guarantor—someone who will make sure that we will never stop learning the Torah and keeping its mitzvos. After a few suggestions which Hashem turned down, we children were nominated as guarantors—and Hashem gladly accepted.” “What are you saying, Sruli?” He asked. “Since the Jewish people only got the Torah because of us children in the first place, this Yom Tov is kind of like our special party! And this being the case, I think it’s perfectly appropriate that we should work on inviting the guests ourselves.” “Bravo, Sruli! The more I get to know you chayolim, the more I’m impressed by your energy and devotion.” As our conversation continued, Mr. Mikhailov and I sorted out some more details. Turns out

he didn’t mean the biggest ice cream party in just one location, rather, a world-wide party wherever Jewish people live, work, and play. (Naturally…I should’ve known as much!) And here’s the coolest part—how we actually invited everyone: First, we compiled a guest list of every single Yid we could possibly involve on this special day. This was done quite simply—a call- text-email center was quickly put together, and we reached out to every shul and Jewish club we could find, asking them to please share the Aseres Hadibros kriah times and locations with their entire mailing lists, along with ice cream orders to be delivered to their groups. However, since there are sadly many Yidden who aren’t involved with a shul or club, and couldn’t be reached to come hear the Aseres Hadibros through these mailing lists, Mr. Mikhailov and I came up with a unique idea. We arranged for every Tzivos Hashem base to receive a giant shipment of boxes: Several refrigerated boxes (i.e. special containers designed to keep things frozen for a long time) containing the most amazing Cholov Yisroel ice-cream-on-a- cone imported from Eretz Yisroel; another box was stuffed with a huge assortment of awesome- flavored toppings, serving utensils and napkins; and in the final box was a portable cooler and a few lightweight folding chairs. We were determined to whip up the most incredible lead-up to Aseres Hadibros ever experienced. Bases worked hard organizing roles and coordinating routes for what would be the first-of-its-kind method of Shavuos mivtzoyim. Finally, Shavuos arrived! After an invigorating night of saying Tikkun Leil Shavuos, Chayolim across the world met up with their local teams at 8:00 am (after a brief sleep), and then

excitedly hit the streets with the clearly branded ice cream coolers, all necessary ingredients, and of course, stacks of maps highlighting every shul in the area and their Aseres Hadibros times. (Many bases even arranged with shuls to provide extra-early and extra-late Torah readings, to accommodate the not-yet- frum families still planning to attend school or work that day.) Chayolim positioned themselves on sidewalk benches, while others brought folding chairs to busy street corners, where they set up their cooler station. “FIND OUT WHERE TO HEAR THE TEN COMMANDMENTS!'' yelled out a few chayolim of the group. Others shouted, “GET YOUR SHAVUOS ICE CREAM HERE! TEN DIFFERENT TOPPINGS TO CHOOSE FROM!” Tens of Jewish mothers, fathers, and their children crowded around the coolers. And that’s when the fun really started! Chayolim instantly got into position, some handing out the ice cream—after carefully opening the wrappers to help recipients avoid ripping letters on Yom Tov—while others sprinkled on the toppings, and the rest of the team explained to families about the importance for every Jewish man, woman, and child to hear the Aseres Hadibros on Shavuos Day (while handing them the mapped-out shul directions, of course). After 2 hours of this electrifying mivtzoyim, chayolim rushed to shul for the main minyan at 10:00 am and to hear the Aseres Hadibros read properly, followed by a yummy milchig kiddush. We eagerly returned to our mivtzoyim posts during the afternoon hours as well, encouraging any Yidden who didn’t yet hear the Aseres Hadibros to attend the specially- arranged afternoon leinings. What can I say, we simply had

the time of our lives on that Yom Tov day as we proudly carried out the Rebbe’s work! Every so often, whenever I had a moment to pause, I’d look up at the Jewish parents and children walking off. I could feel my whole being fill with joy at their eager faces, each proceeding to fulfill today’s special mitzvah in a most glowing and delightful way. And during the hours spent tending to those ice cream coolers, my fellow chayolim and I exchanged many happy glances, feeling so grateful for the zechus to fulfill the Rebbe’s order-of-the-day so thoroughly. I can only imagine how lucky Mr. Mikhailov must have felt at his great privilege of funding this mivtzah! It truly was the best Shavuos of my life. I mean, where else could a boy like me get to use my creativity, energy, and excitement to the fullest, all while doing what Hashem wants, if not for mivtzoyim?! As I lay in bed on Motzei Yom Tov, I wondered how many other children like me have awesome mivtzoyim adventures to share. Chayolim who come up with out-of-this-world ideas and ways to inspire others, doing what it takes to bring Moshiach. The more I thought about it, the more I was convinced that they’re out there, way more than the world knows. And next year, I’m gonna find them!

Do you have a mivtzoim adventure to share? We want to hear it!

Send it to mivtzoyim@tzivoshashem.org and maybe you’ll get

published too, to inspire others- just like Sruli! 10 533שָׁ ֹו ע ּוב 11
